items.title: Fibres of the strict henselization of the normalization and the minimal primes over the algebraic closure of the residue field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a local ring (A, m, kappa) with finitely many minimal primes, lets A' be the integral closure of A in the total ring of fractions of A_red, and considers the maps Spec(A') <- Spec((A')^{sh}) -> Spec(A^{sh}) where (A')^{sh} = A' tensor_A A^{sh}, the strict henselization being taken with respect to a separable algebraic closure kappa^{sep} of kappa inside an algebraic closure; it then asserts three things: that for a maximal ideal m' of A' the residue field kappa' is algebraic over kappa and the fibre of c over m' can be canonically identified with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar); that the right arrow is bijective on minimal primes; and that every minimal prime of (A')^{sh} lies in a unique maximal ideal and every maximal ideal contains a unique minimal prime (source lines 31338-31362). The proof first removes nilpotents: since (A/I)^{sh} = A^{sh}/IA^{sh} for the ideal I of nilpotents and the spectra involved agree, one may assume A is reduced (proof lines 31364-31373). Part (1) is then a computation: kappa'/kappa is algebraic because A' is integral over A, and by going up every maximal ideal of A' or (A')^{sh} lies over the corresponding maximal ideal; the proof computes (A')^{sh} tensor_{A^{sh}} kappa^{sep} = (A' tensor_A kappa) tensor_kappa kappa^{sep}, so the fibre of c over m' is the spectrum of kappa' tensor_kappa kappa^{sep}, and that spectrum is in bijection with Hom_kappa(kappa', kappa-bar) via the map sending sigma to the kernel of sigma tensor 1 (proof lines 31376-31396). Part (3) argues that A' is a finite product of normal domains, that (A')^{sh} is a filtered colimit of etale A'-algebras and hence normal, so every local ring of (A')^{sh} is a normal domain and every maximal ideal contains a unique minimal prime; then the integral-over-henselian-pair lemma makes ((A')^{sh}, m(A')^{sh}) a henselian pair and the connectedness lemma shows the intersection of V(q) with V(m (A')^{sh}) is connected, while V(m (A')^{sh}) = Spec((A')^{sh} tensor kappa^{sh}) is profinite, giving the unique maximal ideal above q (proof lines 31399-31422). Part (2) compares minimal primes of A' with those over minimal primes of A, uses flatness and quasi-finiteness of the filtered colimit to identify them, and finishes with the computation (A')^{sh} tensor_A Q(A) = A^{sh} tensor_A Q(A), where Q(A) is the total fraction ring, observing that the spectra of these two rings are exactly the minimal primes of (A')^{sh} and of A^{sh} respectively (proof lines 31425-31450). The non-routine content is the fibre computation in part (1), the henselian-pair connectedness argument in part (3), and the two-sided minimal-prime comparison in part (2).
